hints: Identify the centre of the circle $(x - 1)^2 + (y + 2)^2 = 25$ as $(1, -2)$.
Use the gradient formula between $(1, -2)$ and $P(4, 2)$: $m = \dfrac{2 - (-2)}{4 - 1}$.
walkthrough:
Find the radius direction before turning through a right angle.
Extract centre $C(1, -2)$ from the circle equation $(x - 1)^2 + (y + 2)^2 = 25$:
$$C = (1, -2)$$

Calculate the gradient of the radius $CP$ connecting $(1, -2)$ to $P(4, 2)$:
$$m_{\text{rad}} = \dfrac{2 - (-2)}{4 - 1} = \dfrac{4}{3}$$

hints: The tangent gradient is perpendicular to the radius gradient: $m_\perp = -\dfrac{1}{4/3} = -\dfrac{3}{4}$.
Rearrange to integer form $ax + by = c$: $4y - 8 = -3x + 12 \implies 3x + 4y = 20$.
walkthrough:
Find the radius direction before turning through a right angle.
The tangent is perpendicular to the radius $CP$:
$$m_{\text{tan}} = -\dfrac{1}{4/3} = -\dfrac{3}{4}$$

Form the equation of the tangent passing through $P(4, 2)$:
$$y - 2 = -\dfrac{3}{4}(x - 4)$$
$$4(y - 2) = -3(x - 4)$$
$$4y - 8 = -3x + 12 \implies 3x + 4y = 20$$
